about: Shared fixture between portico-ha (server) and portico-app (client) for DEV-798 (SEC-02): Home Assistant proves itself to an enrolled phone before the phone sends it a token over a cleartext address. portico-app vendors this file byte for byte and pins its sha256 (the same rule as enroll_v1.json). A change here is a contract bump on both sides.

body.nonce: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$ (made by the app for every probe, never reused)
body.hint: ^[0-9a-f]{16}$ (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of the phone's refresh token, as lowercase hex)

request.rules: Exactly these two fields. Anything else is a 400.

body.proof: 64 lowercase hex: HMAC-SHA256(key = the refresh token as UTF-8, message = "portico-whoami-v1" NUL nonce NUL hint, nonce and hint as ASCII)

refusal.note: One answer for a malformed body, an unknown hint and a revoked token. A 415 for any content type but application/json.

client_rules: Send no token (no Authorization header, no refresh token in the body) in this request.
Verify the proof in constant time against the proof computed from the phone's own refresh token.
On any other outcome (a refusal, a bad proof, a timeout, no refresh token held) treat the address as UNVERIFIED: send no token to it, and use the tailnet.
A phone with no refresh token (enrolled the old format-1 way) has no proof; treat it as unverified.
